markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least two of the student's own logged Seed Lab readings (conditions and plant heights, e.g. 'bright window 30 ml = 8.5 cm; dim shade 30 ml = 4.7 cm; dark cupboard = 1.0 cm') as evidence.
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine readings consistent with the student's own Investigation Record rows; exact wording not required.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('plants grow taller with light') with no logged readings quoted.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why the unfair test cannot show the cause: it changed two variables (light AND water) at once so you cannot tell which caused the difference, whereas a fair test changes only one variable and keeps the others controlled.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct statement that changing more than one thing makes the cause unclear, and that a fair test changes one thing and controls the rest.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only 'the unfair test was wrong' or 'it was not fair' with no reference to changing two variables or to cause.

markingScheme.criterion: States a conclusion supported by the student's own fair-test heights (e.g. brighter light gave taller plants, or a medium amount of water gave the tallest plant) and links it to the evidence.
markingScheme.accept: Any conclusion that matches the student's own fair-test readings and is linked to them.
markingScheme.insufficient: A conclusion with no reference to the data, or one that contradicts the student's own readings.

markingScheme.criterion: States what would be changed (the independent variable: wearing the wristband or not) and what would be measured (the dependent variable: jump height, e.g. in cm).
markingScheme.accept: Any clear independent variable (with/without the wristband) and a measurable outcome (jump height, distance, number of jumps).
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only 'test it' or 'see if it works' with no variable named and no measurement.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains how the test would be kept fair: same people, same jumping surface and effort, and repeated trials (or an average), changing only the wristband.
markingScheme.accept: Any one clear fairness control such as the same person, the same surface, the same effort, or repeating the jump several times.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying 'make it fair' without saying how, or changing more than one thing at once.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains that it counts as real science only if the claim can be tested and the idea is changed or dropped when the evidence disagrees; pseudoscience ignores contrary evidence or cannot be tested.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct reference to testability, empirical evidence, or changing the claim when results disagree.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying 'it is science if it is true' or 'because scientists say so' with no mention of testing or evidence.
